stories.label: Iran war Day 18: Trump 'we won'; Qatar struck; Iran 9 missiles at Al Udeid; Oslo attack aftermath
stories.summary: Day 18. Trump declared 'we won' while saying the US does not want to leave early — a domestic face-saving claim contradicted by ongoing strikes. Iran fired 9 missiles at Qatar — home of Al Udeid Air Base, CENTCOM's forward HQ — eliminating the last diplomatic neutral in the region. Hezbollah simultaneously fired rockets at 5 Israeli bases. 58 Iranian mine-laying ships destroyed per Pentagon. The war is now explicitly targeting Gulf civilian and diplomatic infrastructure.

stories.label: Hormuz economic fallout: SPR tapped; South Korea chips surge 55%; IEA reserves activated
stories.summary: Trump announced a unilateral US SPR drawdown for domestic fuel price relief, coming within hours of the IEA activating one-third of all strategic reserves — dual mobilisation of the entire Western emergency energy system. South Korea's chip exports surged 55.6% in the first 10 days of March: the semiconductor economy, bypassing Hormuz via Pacific routes, is booming while the energy economy collapses. The two-speed global economy is now visible.

stories.label: Sudan/South Sudan: RSF drones expand to Kordofan + Blue Nile; RSF proxies kill 169 in South Sudan
stories.summary: RSF has expanded its drone campaign to Kordofan and Blue Nile (new fronts) and its proxy militias have killed at least 169 in South Sudan — the war has crossed international borders. Hemedti is using the Iran war media blackout to regionalise his control. The crisis now threatens South Sudan's fragile stability. AU/IGAD response unknown.

stories.label: Ecuador targets 'criminal economy' with Trump backing — Latin America US security architecture
stories.summary: Ecuador preparing sweeping crackdown on criminal economy (port logistics, money laundering, fuel theft) with explicit Trump administration backing. A new US security partnership in Latin America distinct from the Milei economic model. Unclear what the US gets in return — watch for basing rights, intelligence sharing, or mining concessions.

stories.label: Africa fungal diseases summit: 1.5M annual deaths finally elevated to public health priority
stories.summary: Landmark summit in Africa formally elevated fungal diseases to public health priority. 1.5M annual deaths — more than malaria — primarily driven by HIV immunosuppression. Nearly invisible in global health coverage. WHO added fungi to priority pathogen list in 2022 but funding has not followed.

stories.label: Eskom sells surplus solar power to Bitcoin miners — African energy grid intersects crypto
stories.summary: Eskom — after years of rolling blackouts — now has surplus midday solar power and plans to sell it to Bitcoin miners. Reveals the structural consequence of rapid solar deployment: surpluses and shortages at different times of day, with Bitcoin mining as buyer of last resort for stranded electricity. South Africa becoming a node in global crypto mining infrastructure.

stories.label: eGFR race adjustment removed — more Black Americans accessing kidney transplants
stories.summary: The eGFR racial coefficient systematically overestimated kidney function in Black patients, keeping them off transplant waitlists for longer than white patients with identical actual kidney function. Removing the race adjustment directly increased the number of Black Americans qualifying for transplants. A named mechanism, named harm, named remedy — algorithmic medicine's bias made concrete.

stories.label: Bellingcat satellite imagery verifies strikes on Iranian civilian infrastructure
stories.summary: Bellingcat has now published two tools/methodologies for Iran war accountability: Turnstone (open-source flight tracking) and satellite imagery analysis showing strikes on Iranian police stations. Together they form an open-source accountability infrastructure for a war where military press offices control information. The satellite methodology is now applicable to the Resalat school strike (168 children).
